questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

If I hand her a flower and say, “Give it to mamma,” she __take it __to her mother.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is written in the** present tense**, as indicated by the phrase “If I hand her a flower and say...”
 
• The verb should be in the **present tense** to match the rest of the sentence.
 
• The correct present tense form of the verb is **"takes"** to ensure subject-verb agreement with the singular subject "she".
 
• Other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **“Was taking it” **uses the **past continuous tense**, which does not match the present tense context of the sentence.
 
• **“Had took it”** and **“Had taken it” **use the **past perfect tense**, which is also not consistent with the** present tense **context of the sentence.
 
 

Therefore, the correct statement is "*If I hand her a flower and say, “Give it to mamma,” she takes it to her mother."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When expressing actions that are happening in the present or are regular occurrences, the** present simple tense **is used.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *If he calls me, I **answer** the phone.*
 
• *When she feels hungry, she **eats** an apple.*

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

__To much__ seriousness __hardens the world, pinning__ it down __with rules__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase **"to much" is incorrect.**
 
• The correct phrase should be** "too much" (intensifier + noun), indicating an excessive amount.**
 
• **"To" **is a preposition, whereas **"too" **means** "excessively"** or** "more than enough," **which suits the context.
 
• **"Too much"** is used to quantify non-count nouns when expressing an excessive amount.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• She had** too much** homework to finish in one night.
 
• He drank** too much **coffee and couldn’t sleep.
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is : ***Too much seriousness hardens the world, pinning it down with rules.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Other options are correctly structured:**

 
• **"With rules"** is correct and does not require any rectification.
 
• **"Hardens the"** is grammatically correct.
 
• **"World, pinning" **is correctly punctuated and grammatical.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rishi asked Karan __will he get a new football for him?__

options.text: would he get a new football for him?
if he would get a new football for him.
if would he get a new football for him?
if he will get a new football for him?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the segment **"asked Karan will he get a new football for him" is incorrect.**
 
• The **correct** form should be **"asked Karan if he would get a new football for him."**
 
• Usage of** "if"** and** the correct order of modal verbs "if he would"** make the sentence **grammatically correct.**
 
• When converting direct speech into **reported speech, modal verbs** often change:
 
• **"Will" changes to "would."**
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Direct: "Will you help me?"
 
• Indirect: He asked if I would help him.
 
 
 
• It's important to ensure that the tense and structure align correctly in reported speech.​

Therefore, the correct statement is **"*Rishi asked Karan if __he would get a new football for him."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Other options are incorrect or unnecessary:

 
• "Would he get a new football for him?" is incorrect because it mistakes the interrogative format.
 
• "If would he get a new football for him?" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• "If he will get a new football for him?" is incorrect because "would" is the appropriate modal verb in reported speech.

• **"Cry over spilt milk" **refers to the act of lamenting or being upset over something that has already occurred and cannot be undone. (बीती बात पर पछताना)
 
 
• **Example: **After losing the game, he realized it was pointless to **cry over spilt milk **and started preparing for the next match.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

If I __will get__ good marks, my father will buy me a laptop.
questions.solution:

__
 
• In English, the first conditional follows the structure: If + present simple, will + base form of the verb.
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'If I will get good marks' is incorrect.
 
• The appropriate form is 'If I get good marks'.

Hence, the correct sentence is **"*If I get__ good marks, my father will buy me a laptop."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Conditional sentences describe the result of a certain condition. In first conditionals, the condition is possible and likely to happen in the future.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• ***If it rains tomorrow, we will stay indoors.***
 
• ***If he studies hard, he will pass the exam.***
 
 
 
• The use of the present simple tense in the 'if' clause helps to accurately reflect a real and possible condition.
